To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a new class of small molecule protein-DNA dimentizers that mimic the function of natural developmental regulators.
a polyamide-peptide construct is designed that binds to a cognate site with a Kd in the low nM range.
a polyamide-peptide hybrid is designed which binds cooperatively with Exd to a specific DNA site.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of molecules that can bind DNA and protein sequence specifically, and can recruit the protein to a DNA site.
the design and synthesis of artificial DNA binding ligands, and the development of novel applications of these compounds.
the design of small molecule regulators of protein-DNA interactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the conjugate is an artificial developmental regulator, which recruits sequence specifically Exd to a target DNA site, with the potential for applications in developmental control and gene therapy.
this work has shown that the Exd-Ubx heterodimer is a modular protein-DNA complex that can be reconstituted in vitro with two small molecules.
a polyamide-peptide construct has been designed that mimics the function of a protein-DNA interaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have designed a small molecule which mimics a protein-protein interaction, in particular the interaction between the Hox cofactor Extradenticle and its cognate DNA site in Drosophila melanogaster.
the artificial dimerizer is a molecular mimic of the Hox protein cofactors Exd/Ubx and that this mimic is able to induce the cooperative binding of Exd/Ubx to the Hox binding site.
we have shown how to make a protein-DNA complex from two separate sequence specific domains.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DNA binding specificity of a polyamide is not lost upon conjugation to a protein binding domain.
it is possible to recruit a protein to its cognate DNA site by a small molecule, which is a major goal of synthetic biology.
it is possible to design small molecules which recruit sequence-specific proteins to cognate DNA targets, and that these molecules can have high affinities for both the DNA and the protein.
